status: Exploratory raster shape boards. Large filled silhouettes for content containers plus small decorative accents. No final style or production implementation approved.

directions.name: Container 1 — Soft wonky panels
directions.style: FAMILY 1: SOFT UNEVEN RECTANGULAR CONTAINERS. Broad nearly straight sides with slight bowing and rounded irregular corners. Mild off-axis asymmetry, a gently slanted shoulder, one corner a little more swollen, an understated wavy edge. Give all six panels distinct silhouettes while they clearly belong to one family. The wide card feels like an imperfect softened rectangle; taller card has one curved shoulder; square tile has two opposite uneven corner radii; banner has a gentle shallow ripple along one long edge; image container has a slightly pinched lower corner; red callout has one gently projecting rounded side. Keep each usable and calm, no extreme blobs or cloud scallops. Small accents have freehand smooth flowing edges. This direction should feel hand-cut, versatile and straightforward to use as cards and containers.
directions.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create an original SHAPED CONTENT CONTAINER exploration board for Hey Kahani's website. The attached images are abstract shape-language references only. The priority is large FILLED PANELS that can actually hold website text or images: cards, tiles, banners, content frames and callouts. Each needs a broad uninterrupted interior and interesting outer perimeter. Include a small supporting selection of standalone abstract accent shapes as well.

LAYOUT: landscape pure-white canvas. Upper 80 percent: SIX LARGE SOLID FILLED CONTAINERS in a roomy 3-column by 2-row arrangement. Same positions and colours throughout this controlled comparison: top left Kesar Sand #FFF1D6 wide landscape card, top middle Sky Blue #63C3FE taller card, top right Mango Yellow #FECB74 square-ish tile; bottom left Lavender tea #D6C9E4 broad banner, bottom middle Coconut Husk #E6CEAD landscape image-holder silhouette, bottom right Gulab Red #D3000A wide callout. Use proportions that fill each grid cell without crowding; all boundaries fully visible. Each container must have a clean usable central area spanning at least 65 percent of its width and height. Its interesting shape is mostly at its perimeter. Most forms should have broad relatively stable long edges to support rectangular image/text content. Empty interiors, no text, no fake lines of copy, no image inserts, no inner outlines.
Lower 20 percent: one separated row of SIX SMALL RANDOM ABSTRACT ACCENTS in the same contour language: a squiggle, a pebble, an open loop, a burst, a bent strip, an arch. Colours use red, ink #05334A, sky blue, green #2B9863 and yellow. Accents occupy much less visual area than the content panels.

STYLE: entirely 2D opaque flat colour on white. No texture, grain, gradients, shading, shadow, outlines or 3D. All six panels are genuinely filled silhouettes, not hollow frames. No labels, letters, words, logos, numbers or watermarks. No animals, sun faces, flowers, people, leaves, books, kites or other illustrative objects. No icons or confetti. Charming thoughtful imperfect contours, grown from the references, legible enough for a real children's brand website. The family-specific edge grammar below is the variable; hold the layout, colour assignments and content usability constant.

directions.name: Container 2 — Scalloped edges
directions.style: FAMILY 2: BOLD SCALLOPED CONTENT PANELS. Use large broad scallops only on selected edges, with stable flat or gently bowed remaining edges. Top-left landscape card has 3 broad shallow scallops along top and a flat bottom; tall blue card has 3 broad lobes down one side, opposite side straight; yellow square tile has a few very broad unequal rounded lobes around its perimeter with huge solid centre; lavender banner has broad shallow alternating waves on top/bottom; tan image holder has softened stepped/scalloped corners but long stable sides; red callout has one dramatic 3-lobe outer end and a broad rectangular body. Maintain clean roomy centres and no thin appendages. Accents are puffy lobed forms and loops. Clearly more expressive than wonky rectangles, but no tiny decorative frills, postage stamp serrations, flower centres or literal clouds.

directions.name: Container 3 — Playful cutaways
directions.style: FAMILY 3: CHUNKY GEOMETRIC CONTAINERS WITH CUTAWAY CORNERS. Strong broad solid panels, mostly stable sides, softened asymmetrical corner geometry. Each one gets one distinctive peripheral gesture: a broad concave scoop from one corner, one angled chamfer, a shallow stepped shoulder, a recessed curved corner, a little offset tab integrated into a wide body, or one opposing convex/concave pair. Six clearly different silhouettes, never a standard rectangle with four identical corners. No cutouts inside the central content area. No card split into pieces. Broad generous usable centre. Edge geometry echoes the reference's playful wedges, notches and soft corners but interpreted as functional content surfaces. Small accents are chunky irregular wedges, arches and zigzags, mixing curved and softly blunt angular contours. No sharp aggressive spikes, jigsaw puzzle pieces or ticket perforations.

directions.name: Container 4 — Organic arches
directions.style: FAMILY 4: SCULPTURAL ARCH AND ORGANIC CONTAINERS. Broad single solid masses with sweeping asymmetrical curved shoulders, oval-like bulges and one relatively stable baseline/side. Top-left cream landscape card has a shallow domed top and nearly flat base; tall blue card is a generous off-centre arch with softly flattened bottom; yellow tile a broad irregular pebble with an extra-wide centre; lavender banner an elongated gently curved capsule with one thicker end, not a thin ribbon; tan image panel a broad soft trapezoid with an organic curved shoulder; red callout a large softly rounded asymmetrical mass whose base is stable and whose upper outline sweeps gently upward. Make these generously filled content shapes, not rings, rainbow arches, slim boomerangs or random decorative squiggles. Small accents use the more freeform pebble, loop and sweeping-curve vocabulary from the reference. Smooth bold readable contours and meaningful breathing room.
